items.group: - CR-005 / RBQA-F006 / ARCHP-004: git_io.rs reads a blob atomically and safely: `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options :` to get the blob sha, then `git cat-file -t` (must be `blob`) and `git cat-file blob `; reject a rev starting with `-` in parse_extract (both `--rev X` and `--rev=X` forms); accept 40- or 64-hex object ids; classify failures by exit status plus `cat-file -e`, not English stderr (set LC_ALL=C on git calls as belt and braces); same repo-relative path rules as sc-jev-check's validate_relative (reject absolute, `..`, backslash, drive prefix); GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 on every git call. Tests: `--rev=--output=` is rejected before any git call and the file is never created; a moving ref between bytes and sha cannot mismatch (by construction now); a 64-hex sha is accepted. - CR-010: canonicalize the source-path argument (falling back to canonicalizing its parent when the file is absent at WORKTREE) before strip_prefix against the canonicalized toplevel, so `/tmp/...` on macOS works. - ARCHP-007 / QA-006: replace the 2^n cfg LANGUAGES/load arms with one static table `struct Grammar { info, load: fn() -> Language, queries: &'static [Asset] }` with `#[cfg(feature)]` per element; single lookup; remove the unreachable fallback arm; `#[cfg(feature = "python")]` / `"rust"` on every grammar-specific test and on the CLI test asserting both languages; `cargo test -p sc-treesitter --no-default-features`, `--no-default-features --features python`, `--features rust` must all pass. Then flip the CI job in `.github/workflows/sc-agent-ci.yml` from `cargo hack --each-feature check` to `cargo hack --each-feature test -p sc-treesitter` and delete the "check, not test" caveats in that workflow comment and in docs/development/ci.md (these two files are allowed for exactly this edit). - ARCHP-008: convert source to &str once and slice; dead capture-index and span-bounds checks become debug_assert!; skip the error walk when `!root.has_error()`; treat `is_missing()` like `is_error()` for the parse-error rule (add a fixture test with a MISSING node). - ARCHP-010: `#[non_exhaustive]` on LanguageInfo and QueryInfo; `ExtractInput::new(language, query, source)` constructor with setters and non_exhaustive; build QueryInfo from the Asset table by reference (delete the duplicate struct). - ARCHP-011 (bug part only; keep the custom parser): add `--version` / `-V` printing PRODUCER_NAME and CARGO_PKG_VERSION; `--help`/`-h` recognised only in the first two argument slots. Do NOT adopt clap. - ARCHP-012: delete the duplicated `.scm` copy under tests/fixtures/cross-impl/branches/queries/ and the test that compares it (query_sha256 in subjects.json already pins the bytes); fix any fixture loader that read it. - ARCHP-003 routine part: a missing positional argument becomes InputInvalid (not InputMissing with the check.toml hint); span/line overflow becomes ExtractionFailed or InputInvalid with a detail (not InputTooLarge); stdout write failure vs git spawn failure get distinct details via JevError::io_failed. - QA-005: the one rustdoc warning in sc-treesitter (lib.rs:4 SubjectsDocument link) → 0. - FTQ-003 (treesitter part): test git helpers set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null (NUL on Windows) and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0; subprocess tests use a deadline helper like sc-ai's spawn_with_deadline (copy it into the crate's test support; sharing across crates is D7).

- ARCHP-013: build_request runs under `py.detach(move || build(...))` with owned arguments; test that a Python thread progresses while a slow command extractor runs (use a scripted sleep command with a short timeout). - ARCHP-015: `struct LoggerInner(Logger)` with Drop { flush; shutdown }; LoggerGuard holds Arc; delete the strong_count check. - ARCHP-016: process-wide `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<PathBuf, Weak>>>` keyed by canonical log root so one Logger/writer per log file is reused across run_check calls in one interpreter; test that two runs in one process share one writer. - ARCHP-017 / EXT-003 / RBP-F013 (parsing part): parse backends with `BackendId::from_str` (wave 1) — decide and document: kebab-case aliases are NOT accepted (matches sc-ai and the engine; same INPUT_INVALID code); parse revs with `Rev::parse`; resolve_repo checks is_dir and absolutizes like sc-ai; delete utf8_payload and the local backend/rev parsers; update tests/fixtures/jev-python tests that asserted the old alias/CONFIG_INVALID behaviour. Use `RunOptions::dry_run_only` (wave 2) so dry-run creates no session store or logger. - EXT-003 / ARCHP-018: ONE `run_check` pyfunction signature — scripted-answer injection moves to a `_testing` submodule registered only under the test-util feature (`sc_jev_py._testing.run_check_scripted`), and the Python tests use it; make the pyfunctions/pyclasses pub(crate) and drop the `pub use` lines from lib.rs; crate-type cdylib only (keep unit tests building — if `cargo test -p sc-jev-py` needs rlib, keep rlib but stop re-exporting); `#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "Python keyword API")]` replacing the three `#[allow]`s; `[lints] workspace = true` for sc-jev-py with an override only where PyO3 macros need it (wave 1 left this crate out). - ARCHP-019 (routine subset): accept `Option` for every path parameter (PyO3 extracts str and os.PathLike) and return path helpers as `PathBuf`; `#[pyclass(frozen)]` on the immutable classes; convert outcomes/equal_input to Python objects once at construction instead of re-encoding JSON per getter; remove `CheckResult.ask` in favour of `Session.ask` ONLY if the Python tests do not depend on it — otherwise keep and document; ship `sc_jev_py.pyi` and `py.typed` in the wheel (pyproject/maturin config), covering the single run_check signature, build_request, CheckResult, Session, JevError. Do NOT change the error exception class design. - ARCHP-020 routine part: delete the duplicate cross-impl fixture comparison at run.rs:~725-737 (tests/jev_cross_impl is the owner); leave the [[test]] hosting where it is (moving it is D7/r-3b). - ARCHP-021: tempfile::TempDir in sc-jev-py tests (incl. logging.rs); no leak on panic. - ARCHP-022: move the scripted-answer string-shorthand normalisation into sc-jev-check's `register_scripted_backends` (test-util) so CLI and Python accept the same shape; the binding only forwards. - FTQ-002: pure `default_log_root_from(home: Option, tmp: &Path)` with the production wrapper reading env; test both branches with injected inputs; the Python twin test (test_module_documents_log_root) made env-independent via monkeypatch. - QA-005: the five rustdoc warnings in sc-jev-py → 0. - QA-008: no unguarded `.expect` on data in library code; invariant expects keep a unit test proving the invariant (ServiceName/TargetCategory constants in logging.rs).

- `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` must emit 0 warnings; then remove `continue-on-error: true` from the `doc` job in `.github/workflows/sc-agent-ci.yml` and delete the matching "Known limits" bullet in docs/development/ci.md (QA-005 removal condition). - Add a repo `.gitattributes` pinning byte-compared fixtures to LF (`tests/fixtures/** -text` plus `*.scm -text`, `*.json text eol=lf` under fixtures, or `* text=auto eol=lf` if the whole tree is LF-safe — check with `git ls-files --eol`); then remove the five `Keep LF line endings` steps from sc-agent-ci.yml and the ci.md note, and delete the corresponding "Phase close notes" open item in docs/plans/phase-a/plan.md (FTQ-005 / REQ-QA-A10-005 / QA-003 follow-up). Verify the sc-treesitter golden-byte test still passes after a fresh `git checkout` of the fixture. - Merge origin/integrate/phase-a again if it moved (check `git log HEAD..origin/integrate/phase-a`).

cursor-fix-task.acceptance-criteria: - `just lint`, `just test`, `just test-python` (fresh venv), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` with ZERO warnings, `cargo hack --each-feature test -p sc-treesitter` (install cargo-hack if missing), `bash scripts/sc-publish-dry-run.sh` exit 0, `cargo test --workspace` twice. - pytest tests/fixtures/jev-python passes against a wheel built with `--features extension-module,test-util`; the `.pyi` is in the wheel; `python -c "import sc_jev_py; help(sc_jev_py.run_check)"` shows one signature. - Every security item has a test that fails without the fix (option-injection rev, symlink/outside path on macOS /tmp). - No D-scope entered (list anything you believe is an architectural decision in disguise instead); no ADR text; no kit-written files; CI/docs edits limited to the three named (feature matrix flip, doc continue-on-error removal, LF steps removal + .gitattributes). - Commit per group (A, B, C) with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 ` (this is the attribution the repository owner requires for this session; use it verbatim), push, report pushed SHA, per-item status table, validation table incl. rustdoc count before/after and coverage for sc-jev-py (`cargo llvm-cov -p sc-jev-py --summary-only`, target ≥ 75%), and the GitHub `sc-agent-ci` run result on the pushed SHA.
